chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: The Mack David family's big band rehearses next door
summary: Neighbours in Houston, the sons of Dr. Mack David, ran a big jazz band that rehearsed at home, and he listened in and bought a cheap five-and-dime drum.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Which I did jump a little something there.
Yeah, go back.
About the Mac David Brothers. We were living next door to them.
When was this, in Beaumont?
No, this was in Houston.
Yeah.
Well, they had a big band, and they rehearsed -- a jazz band, see.
You lived next door to people that had a --
I didn't know it. He was a doctor, really, Dr. Mac David. And he had two sons which -- they were grown. I was a young kid. And when they would have rehearsals, well, I could hear it.
They'd rehearse in the house.
Yes. And they liked me, and I would go over there and ask them, could I listen. And I would listen to them rehearsing.
That must have been very satisfying.
That was very great for me.
Yeah.
And I just wished that I could play with them.
Yeah.

And I'd get my sticks and I went downtown and bought me a little drum in the five and ten cents store, which it had sheepskin on one side, and on the other side was paper, really, like paper sacking, you know?
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
And it had some little strings running in the back. And I would sit over there and play on this. Just to be playing.
Yeah, to be able to get some rhythms going.
